chief_complaint: inability to maintain erection for intercourse
hpi_details: A 38-year-old male presents to the clinic with inability to maintain erection for intercourse. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks overwhelming work hours and chronic burnout have completely drained his testosterone and physical stamina.
concerns: He is worried that this issue is creating emotional distance with his partner and could end up destroying their marriage.
expectations: He hopes to have his hormone levels checked and receive a prescription for performance pills to restore his confidence.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Erectile Dysfunction is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Management addresses reversible cardiovascular, endocrine, medication, and psychosocial contributors; a PDE5 inhibitor may be considered only after reviewing cardiovascular fitness and contraindicated nitrate or riociguat use.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: inability to maintain erection for intercourse
Key HPI features: a 38-year-old man reports recently worsening difficulty maintaining an erection for intercourse with generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Erectile Dysfunction.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Erectile Dysfunction.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Urinary tract infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Missing priapism, acute neurologic symptoms, or exertional chest pain that requires urgent assessment.
management_principles: Assess cardiovascular risk, medication and substance contributors, and psychosocial factors; obtain morning testosterone when symptoms suggest hypogonadism, and consider a PDE5 inhibitor only when safe.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of inability to maintain erection for intercourse. HPI: erectile dysfunction.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Erectile Dysfunction.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Erectile Dysfunction.
reference_soap.plan: Assess cardiovascular risk and medication, substance, endocrine, and psychosocial contributors. Check morning testosterone if low libido or other features suggest hypogonadism. Discuss a PDE5 inhibitor only after confirming no nitrate or riociguat use and adequate cardiovascular fitness; provide lifestyle counseling and follow-up.

must_ask.objective: Onset pattern - gradual vs sudden, situational vs global
must_ask.say: Did this come on gradually over time, or suddenly, and does it happen in every situation or only sometimes?
Do you have diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or a history of heart disease?
Are you taking any blood pressure or antidepressant medications, and do you smoke, drink alcohol, or use recreational drugs?

must_ask.objective: Presence of morning erections and libido
must_ask.say: Do you still get erections when you wake up in the morning, and has your sex drive changed?
Have you been under a lot of stress, anxiety, or relationship difficulties recently?

history.answer: I have been having trouble getting and keeping an erection strong enough for intercourse lately.
This started about three months ago and has been gradually getting worse since then.
The trouble is strictly with getting firm down there; I do not have any pain, numbness, or tingling radiating anywhere.
Sometimes I can start to get an erection, but it quickly loses firmness before or right after penetration. Most of the time now, I cannot complete intercourse at all.
It happens almost every time my partner and I try to be intimate, and it has definitely become more frequent over the past month.
It seems worse when I am exhausted or stressed from work. Taking a warm shower or resting helps me relax, but it does not fix the erection.
I have felt constantly fatigued and run-down lately, but I have not had any fevers, chills, or night sweats.
I used to wake up with an erection most mornings, but over the last couple of months, that has dwindled to maybe once every few weeks or not at all.
My sexual drive has definitely dropped a bit over the last few months along with feeling so tired all the time.
The problem happens in all situations, whether I am with my partner or trying to masturbate on my own.
No, I do not get any chest pain, tightness, shortness of breath, or heart racing, even when I walk up stairs.
No, I have not had any weakness in my legs, loss of balance, or loss of feeling around my groin or buttocks.
No, my urination is completely normal. I do not have burning, weak stream, hesitance, or waking up frequently at night to pee.
No, I have never had an erection that stayed hard for hours or caused pain.
No fever, unintended weight loss, chills, or visible blood anywhere.
I have never had erection problems like this before, and I have never been evaluated or treated for sexual health issues.
I tried resting more on weekends and bought an herbal stamina supplement online a few weeks ago, but it did not make any difference.
Nothing unusual like chemical exposures or recent travel, just long work hours at my desk.
It has created frustration and tension in my relationship, and I feel down on myself. I also have trouble sleeping well because of stress.
Work has been demanding lately, and this issue definitely adds stress between me and my partner, though she tries to be supportive.
I thought maybe working eighty hours a week and constant burnout have just wiped out my testosterone and stamina.
I'm terrified that my wife thinks I'm not attracted to her anymore and that this is going to destroy our marriage.
I'm hoping to get my hormone levels tested and maybe get a prescription like Viagra to help me get through this rough patch.
I have always been healthy. I have never been diagnosed with high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or thyroid problems.
I have never had any surgeries, major injuries, or hospital stays.
I do not take any prescription medications.
No, I have never used chest pain pills like nitroglycerin, and I do not use recreational drugs, cannabis, or anabolic steroids.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I do not smoke cigarettes or use any tobacco products, and I never have.
I only have one or two beers on the weekend socially, never heavy drinking.
I work as an office manager, mostly at a desk, and I live with my long-term partner.
My father was diagnosed with mild high blood pressure in his sixties, but there is no early heart disease, stroke, or hormonal disease in my family.
I am in a monogamous relationship with my female partner; I have never had a sexually transmitted infection.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Well-developed, alert male in no acute distress; normal secondary male sex characteristics without gynecomastia.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal heart sounds; no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs heard.
Clear to auscultation bilaterally; normal breath sounds with no wheezes or crackles.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and flat; no palpable masses, organomegaly, or aortic bruits.
Bilateral femoral, popliteal, and dorsalis pedis pulses are intact, symmetric, and 2+ throughout.
Normal circumcised phallus without fibrous plaques, lesions, or urethral discharge; both testes are descended with normal size and consistency and no masses or tenderness.
Normal anal sphincter tone; smooth, symmetric, non-tender prostate of normal volume without nodules.
Intact sensation to light touch and pinprick across perineal, perianal, and lower extremity dermatomes.
Symmetric 2+ deep tendon reflexes at patellar and Achilles tendons; bulbocavernosus reflex is intact.
